alignments.note: Waw of the consecutive form takes the written *And*.
Construct noun takes a supplied *the* under rule 29, the article morpheme on the rectum taking the *the* standing before its own word.
Nomen rectum takes the relational *of* under rule 19.
Article morpheme takes the written *the* standing before its own word; nothing is fronted, since the ASV writes a *the* for each noun (rule 29).
Finite verb; the explicit subject noun phrase carries the subject.
Preposition takes the written *unto*.
Suffix takes the object pronoun under rule 18.
Preposition takes the written *on*.

The article assimilated into the pointed preposition is a real token under rule 12 and takes the phrase's single written *the*; being the first of the phrase's two articles, it is the one that takes it under rule 47.
Noun takes its own word.
Agreement article on the attributive, with the phrase's one *the* already taken by the noun's own article, so `unrepresented` under rule 47.
Ordinal takes its own word.
A preposition standing on `טֶרֶם` rendered by one English word meets rule 30's one-rendering condition, so the pair share a unit headed on the morpheme carrying the lexeme.
Article takes the written *the*.
Noun takes its own word.
Finite verb takes the lexical verb.

Directive `he` tagged `Sd`, which rule 32 aligns to whatever English the ASV spends on the direction; here that is the *down* of *went down*. The competing reading treats *down* as the English verb's phrasal particle under rule 44 and leaves the `he` `unrepresented`, but rule 32 directs that a `Sd` take the directional word where one is written.
Interrogative takes its own word; it is the clause's predicate slot filler with the adjective following.

Verbless clause: the construction-supplied copula joins the adjectival predicate under rule 20, headed on the adjective. The comparative inflection is English's way of writing the `מִן` relation, which keeps its own *than*.
Comparative `מִן` takes the written *than* under rule 24.
Noun takes its own word.
Waw takes the written *and*.
Interrogative takes its own word.
Supplied copula joins the adjectival predicate under rule 20.
Comparative `מִן` takes the written *than*.
The indefinite article belongs to the noun that licenses it under rule 15.
Waw takes the written *And*.
Finite verb with its subject pronoun under rule 17.
Preposition takes the written *unto*.
Suffix takes the object pronoun.

`לוּלֵא` is a single negative conditional particle the ASV writes in two words, *If ... not*, discontinuous around the verb's subject and auxiliary under rule 25; no second negative morpheme stands in this clause for the *not* (the `לֹא` at s037 belongs to the apodosis). Headed on *If*, the word that subordinates the clause; the competing reading heads on *not*, since the negation is what distinguishes `לוּלֵא` from `אִם`.
Finite verb with its subject pronoun and auxiliary under rule 17, discontinuous around the particle's *not*.
Preposition takes the written *with*.
Suffix takes the possessive under rule 18.
Noun takes its own word.
Negative of the apodosis takes the written *not*.
Finite verb with subject and auxiliary under rule 17; *out* is the English verb's phrasal particle and stays with it, as rule 44 states for `מָצָא` → *find out*.
Suffix takes the possessive.
Noun takes its own word.

review_notes: *the men of the city* writes a *the* before each noun, so nothing is fronted under rule 29: the article morpheme takes the *the* standing before its own word and the construct takes a supplied one.
`בְּטֶרֶם` is fused on the single *before* under rule 30 and headed on `טֶרֶם`, which carries the lexeme.
`לוּלֵא` is read as one morpheme rendered discontinuously by *If ... not*; the head choice between the two words is named in the unit's note.
